**Dropnook 2.0.1** — fixes from a full code review and pen test.

* **Drop answers only to its own names.** It now answers to IP addresses, local names (`tower.local`, `….lan`, `….fritz.box`), the names of its certificates and `WEBUI` from the `.env`, and nothing else. This closes a DNS-rebinding hole: on a Drop without PIN and without HTTPS, a web site opened in your network could have read and changed it.
  **If you open Drop under a domain without HTTPS:** put that name into `WEBUI` in the `.env` (on Unraid: *Edit Stack* → *.env*) and take the new `compose.yaml`, which passes `WEBUI` on. Opened with HTTPS, by IP address or under a local name, nothing changes.
* **Security headers on Drop's own page:** no other site may frame it or embed its files.
* **Certificate renewals were not picked up while an interrupted upload was left over,** so the certificate could expire. Now an upload without progress for 10 minutes no longer holds a renewal back, and is given up after 7 days.
* **Limits against crashes:** an upload has to fit the free space, a text field holds up to 2 million characters, and requests are read only up to a size.
* **Resuming an upload** now also compares when the file was last changed. A changed file of the same name and size starts over instead of being mixed with the old one.
* **File names made over SMB** (from a Mac, with a backslash, or not in UTF-8) no longer break downloads or the file list. Two uploads with the same name that finish at the same moment no longer overwrite each other.
* **A new share** could, rarely, be tidied away while it was being created.
* **PIN guessing is counted per PIN:** signing in with your own PIN no longer resets the count for someone else's. `SHARING=off` no longer switches off the guard against requests through a proxy, and more proxy headers are recognised.
* **Smaller fixes:**
  * Tabs open for different users load the right pictures and downloads.
  * The connection dot turns grey when live updates stop.
  * Share passwords are hashed with 600 000 rounds; older links keep working.
  * Malformed requests get 400 instead of 500.

**Updating:** *Check for Updates* → *Update*. If you open Drop under a domain without HTTPS, see the first point.
